info.description:
Read-only access to the CONFIDENTIA platform's metadata store and its
disclosure-controlled Gold marts.

Every value returned is read from a table or view the pipeline already writes. The
API computes no metrics of its own, holds no key material, and cannot trigger a
pipeline run -- see ADR 0016.

Authentication is a bearer token. Roles form a disclosure ladder:
`viewer` < `operator` < `auditor`.
info.title: CONFIDENTIA API

get.description:
``hardware_rooted`` is returned per row and must be rendered.

Under the ``sim`` backend a measurement is a hash of this repository's source,
not an SGX MRENCLAVE. The policy row carries that distinction so a client cannot
present a simulated attestation as a hardware-rooted one.

schema.title: Response Attestation Policy Audit Attestation Policy Get

get.summary: Which measurements may hold which keys

get.description:
How much of each mart C4 blanked, and why.

``complementary_suppressed`` is the count that matters: primary suppression
alone leaves a small cell recoverable by subtracting the published cells from a
published total, so a mart with primary suppression and no complementary
suppression has usually not been protected.
get.summary: Suppression applied to each published mart

get.description:
Refusals are the interesting rows, so they are not filtered out by default.

An audit log that only records successes cannot answer the question it exists
for. ``granted=false`` isolates the four refusal paths: unknown measurement,
revoked policy, tenant not permitted, and stale or replayed evidence.

schema.title: Response Key Releases Audit Key Releases Get
Response Key Release Summary Audit Key Releases Summary Get

get.description:
Should be empty. Stage 7c took this from 5 to 0, and CI keeps it there.

Kept as an endpoint precisely because it should be empty: a dashboard tile that
is normally blank and occasionally is not is how the next coverage gap gets
noticed before it depresses a recall number in a report.
get.summary: Defect families with no rule at all
Latest P/R/F1 per dataset and defect family

get.description:
Aggregated from the confusion-matrix counts, not by averaging F1.

Averaging per-family F1 weights a family with three defects the same as one with
four hundred. Summing TP/FP/FN and dividing once is the micro-average, and it is
the number that answers "how good is the quality layer on this dataset".

**Two micro-averages are returned, and the second is the honest one.** At Bronze
a duplicate and a legitimate redelivery are byte-identical, so every redelivered
row counts as a false positive for ``duplicate_record`` -- 19,855 of them on
``financial/transaction`` alone, which drags that dataset's precision from 0.84
to 0.14. That number measures the layer's blindness, not the rules.

The exclusion is computed here rather than left to callers. A client that had to
subtract the contaminated family itself would be computing a metric, which is
exactly what ADR 0016 forbids -- and the first client that forgot would publish
0.14 as a result.

get.summary: Datasets the gate is blocking right now

get.description:
A gate nobody can override is a gate that gets disabled the first time it is
wrong at an inconvenient moment. An override is therefore permitted and
recorded -- and this endpoint exists so that "how often is the gate overridden"
is a question with an answer.

``seen_count`` above 1 is the exactly-once guarantee working, not an error.

A batch whose content digest has been presented several times was ingested once
and skipped thereafter. Surfacing the count makes redelivery visible instead of
silent, which matters because silent redelivery and silent data loss look
identical from a row count.
get.summary: Ingest batches and their deduplication state
Rows and bytes ingested per tenant and dataset

get.description:
``watermark_kind`` is returned because the value alone is ambiguous.

An LSN, a timestamp and a file sequence are all opaque strings in this column,
and comparing two of different kinds is meaningless -- which is why the kind is
a discriminator on the row rather than something a client infers from the shape.
get.summary: Current watermark per source and dataset

get.description:
``payload``, ``signature`` and ``public_key_pem`` are omitted here.

The payload names source paths, transformation parameters and record counts for
a tenant's data. Reading it is an audit action, so it is behind the auditor role
on the single-entry endpoint rather than returned fifty at a time by a list.

Auditor-only, and returns the material needed to verify the entry offline.

``payload``, ``signature`` and ``public_key_pem`` together let a third party
recompute the digest and check the signature without trusting this API -- which
is what makes the lineage claim verifiable rather than merely asserted.

schema.title: Response Entry Lineage Entries  Seq  Get

get.summary: One entry, with its signed payload and public key

get.description:
The head digest commits to every entry before it.

An external party who records this value can later detect any edit to any
earlier entry -- which is the entire point of chaining, and the reason it is
viewer-readable while the payloads are not.

Shallow verification: links, signatures, and column-versus-payload agreement.

``deep`` is absent by design, not by omission -- see the module docstring. The
response says so explicitly so that a caller cannot read a passing result as
proof the lake still matches its signed roots. It does not.

schema.title: Response Verify Chain Endpoint Lineage Verify Get

get.description:
Row counts come from ``count(*)`` per table, not from ``reltuples``.

``pg_class.reltuples`` is an estimate maintained by ANALYZE, and these tables
are dropped and recreated on every publish -- so the estimate is frequently -1
or stale by a whole run. There are six marts of a few thousand rows; an exact
count is cheap and a wrong one is confusing.
get.summary: Published marts, with their disclosure record

get.description:
No ORDER BY.

Mart schemas differ and are not known at write time, so there is no column this
router could order by that is guaranteed to exist. An unordered paged read is
honest about that; inventing an order from the first column would produce pages
that shift under the client when the mart is republished. Clients that need a
stable order should fetch the mart whole -- they are thousands of rows, not
millions -- or sort client-side.

Response Mart Schema Marts  Name  Schema Get

get.description:
Unauthenticated on purpose, and therefore carries no operational data.

``tee`` is here because every confidentiality claim this platform makes is
conditional on it. Under the ``sim`` backend the enclave is *modelled*, and a
dashboard that renders "attested" without qualification would be making a claim
the platform cannot support. The label is served from the same setting the
pipeline uses, so the two cannot drift.
get.summary: What this deployment is, and what it is not

get.description:
Joined to ``dq_rule`` so a failure arrives with its description and severity.

Without the join a client gets ``rule_id`` and a pass rate, and has to fetch the
catalogue to render anything -- which every client would then do on every poll.
``redacted_record`` is not selected here. See ``/quarantine/{id}``.

schema.title: Response Quarantine Summary Quality Quarantine Summary Get

get.description:
Auditor-only.

``redacted_record`` had its sensitive fields removed when it was written, which
is not the same as being safe to show anyone: it is still a real row from a real
tenant, and the reason it is here is that something about it was wrong.

schema.title: Response Quarantine Record Quality Quarantine  Quarantine Id  Get

get.summary: One quarantined row, including its redacted contents

get.description:
One row per (tenant, dataset, layer), chosen by ``DISTINCT ON``.

Postgres-specific and deliberately so: the portable alternative is a window
function over the whole table or a correlated subquery, and this table is
written once per pipeline run forever. ``DISTINCT ON`` reads the index.

schema.title: Response Latest Scores Quality Scores Latest Get

get.summary: The most recent score per dataset

get.description: 503 with a body, not an exception, so the body is machine-readable either way.

Newest first. ``error_message`` is deliberately omitted from the list.

A failure message can carry a fragment of the offending record -- a malformed
row echoed back by a driver, for instance -- and the list endpoint is the one a
dashboard polls. It is available on the single-run endpoint, where fetching it
is a deliberate act.

Aggregated in SQL, not in Python.

The alternative -- fetching runs and grouping them here -- would put a second
definition of "failed" in the codebase and would page 621 rows over the wire to
produce six numbers.
